criteria.semantics: A native <section> named by the group's label (aria-label): a region of related content, its children inside it in order.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.
Moves through the group's controls in order.

criteria.name: The group's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the group's content grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the group's content stack in one column, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <section> element.
The group is named by its label in aria-label.
WHEN I move into the group with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name and the role of region.
WHEN I list the landmarks I HEAR the group by its name.

criteria.semantics: The group's children in order (in columns, with the columns hint); it draws nothing of its own. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Group named by its label.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the group by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.
Moves through the group's controls in reading order.

criteria.name: The group's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the group's content grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the group's content drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the group's content at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the group's content drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the group's content whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A group adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the group's children in the order the model gives them, the same as the tab order.
WHEN I move into the group with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its name.

announce.api: AXGroup, its label as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::Group).
ControlType Group, its label as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_PANEL (ATSPI_ROLE_SECTION), its label as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
